fields.title: Polka: the missing hour
fields.summary: A migration script deleted the contents of 3,400 orders. Rolling back restores the data and erases four hours.
fields.decisionPrompt: What do we do? State the price of your decision.
fields.brief/role: You are a product manager at Polka.
fields.brief/company: Polka is a fictional grocery delivery service from local stores: 900 partner stores, a buyer app, and a partner dashboard.
fields.brief/context: You are a product manager at Polka. Yesterday during a schema migration, a faulty script deleted order items for the past 4 hours, leaving 3,400 orders without contents. Restoring from a backup will revert the state to 5 minutes before the work started, but it will also roll back everything that happened over the 4 hours: new orders, profile changes, reviews. You need a decision today.
fields.brief/objective: Restore operations where orders are being assembled without creating a second loss.
fields.brief/constraints: A decision is needed today. Point-in-time recovery takes six hours and has not been tested.
fields.brief/task: Decide what you are doing and explain what you are sacrificing.
fields.learnTakeaway/title: Recovery starts with what is blocking people right now
fields.learnTakeaway/body: A full rollback is a temptingly simple action that almost always trades one loss for another: by restoring the old state, you erase everything that happened after, including money. Separate the lost data into what blocks work right now and what is simply unpleasant. Fix the first by any available means, including manual work; handle the second calmly and correctly.
fields.evidenceCards/0/content: Items for 3,400 orders. The orders themselves, amounts, and statuses are intact—only the contents are lost.
fields.evidenceCards/1/content: 1,900 orders created during this time, profile changes, and 140 reviews will be lost. Payments for these orders have already gone through.
fields.evidenceCards/2/content: "Point-in-time recovery of items from the transaction log is possible, about 6 hours of work, medium risk. Full rollback is 40 minutes, low risk. There is a catalog export from which some order contents can be indirectly restored."
fields.evidenceCards/3/content: The payment provider knows all payments. Stores received order contents via notifications and are assembling them right now.
fields.decisionOptions/0/consequence: the contents of 3,400 orders are restored. 1,900 paid orders disappear—you will have to refund the money or restore them manually. The problem is shifted, not solved: there were 3,400 damaged orders, now there are 1,900 non-existent paid orders.
fields.decisionOptions/1/description: 6 hours, medium risk, procedure has not been tested.
fields.decisionOptions/1/consequence: if it works, there are no losses at all. If not, 6 hours are lost, and 900 orders currently being assembled are left without contents the entire time. According to the rule in `SC3-N5`, an untested procedure will likely fail on the first try.
fields.decisionOptions/2/label: Manually restore 900 active orders using store notifications, the rest from the log
fields.decisionOptions/2/description: Manually restore 900 active orders using store notifications, the rest from the log without rush. 2 hours for active ones, then take it easy.
fields.decisionOptions/2/consequence: the operational problem is resolved in 2 hours—stores assemble using their notifications, contents are entered back. 2,500 delivered orders remain without contents in history—unpleasant, but not blocking. Then tackle the log without time pressure.
fields.decisionOptions/3/label: Rollback plus manual recovery of 1,900 orders using provider data
fields.decisionOptions/3/description: Rollback plus manual recovery of 1,900 orders using provider data. 40 minutes plus days of work.
fields.decisionOptions/3/consequence: complete recovery in the end. Days of manual work, risk of errors, some users will see orders disappear and reappear.
fields.rubric/remediation/0/gap: Fails to distinguish between RPO and product consequences of a rollback
fields.rubric/remediation/1/gap: Does not prepare reconciliation with external systems
fields.rubric/remediation/3/gap: Target reliability is not derived from what the user loses
